title: Two-word stops that take the floor: hold on, wait wait, no stop, one sec

items.speaker: agent
items.text: Thanks for calling. How can I help you today?

items.speaker: caller
items.text: Hi, could you go over what I need to bring to my first visit?

items.speaker: agent
items.text: Yes. For a first visit, please bring a photo ID, such as a passport or a driving licence, a letter or card showing your current address, and a list of anything you are currently taking. If you have a referral letter, bring that as well, and if you were sent any forms to fill in, bring them completed. Arrive ten minutes early so the front desk can check everything in.

items.speaker: caller
items.text: Sorry, I'm writing this down. Go on.

items.speaker: agent
items.text: No problem. Photo ID, proof of address, a list of what you are taking, your referral letter if you have one, and any forms you were sent, filled in.

items.speaker: caller
items.text: What counts as proof of address?

items.speaker: agent
items.text: A recent utility bill, a bank statement or a council letter with your name and address on it, dated within the last three months. A photo of it on your phone is fine as long as the name, address and date are readable, and the front desk can check it without you handing the phone over.

items.speaker: caller
items.text: Okay, got it. Anything else I need?

items.speaker: agent
items.text: Just your appointment confirmation, either printed or on your phone, and that is everything. If you forget something, the front desk can usually sort it out on the day, so do not worry too much.
